Our results suggest that VDER is a promising approach for improving the performance of reinforcement learning agents in complex environments.

This method is based on a buffer that stores the gradients received from the parties, and it uses a combination of asynchronous aggregation and a novel gradient update rule to ensure convergence. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through experiments on a range of datasets and models, including a large-scale image classification task. Our results show that Buffered Asynchronous Aggregation can achieve faster convergence and better performance than existing methods, even when the parties have different data distributions and communication rates. Overall, our method offers a flexible and efficient approach to federated learning that can be applied to a wide range of scenarios.
